entry.content:
1 minute read
TTArtisan AF 12mm f/2.8 ASPH: price and specs
2:14

TTArtisan's AF 12mm f/2.8 ASPH is a full-frame ultra-wide prime for Sony E and Nikon Z. It costs $489, though older Sony bodies have limited support.

TTArtisan has added a 12mm to its growing line of budget autofocus primes. The AF 12mm f/2.8 ASPH covers full frame and is listed for Sony E and Nikon Z mounts at $489.

At 122°, this is properly wide, which suits interiors, architecture, and gimbal work.

Autofocus options at this focal length are still few, which explains why the announcement is getting a decent amount of traction online. The lens uses an STM stepping motor, with eye- and face-detection tracking claimed by the company.

Specs, size, and filter support

The optical formula runs to 16 elements in 10 groups, including two aspherical elements. The aperture runs from f/2.8 to f/16, with six blades and a clicked ring, and the lens focuses down to 0.18 m (7.1 in).

The lens has an 82 mm filter thread, and TTArtisan includes a metal filter holder for standard 82 mm filters, plus a metal cap and hood. Weight is listed as between 336 and 349 g (11.9 to 12.3 oz), which is light for a lens this wide.

TTArtisan's own claims include excellent aberration and distortion control, sharpness from center to edge, minimal focus breathing, and six-point sunstars when stopped down.

Sony E compatibility varies by camera body

Anyone interested needs to pay attention to compatibility, especially for video. TTArtisan says the lens works seamlessly on Nikon Z bodies, but older Sony E cameras have limited functionality. The a7 III is fully compatible for photo modes and only partially for video, and the original a7 and a7 II lack full compatibility. AF performance may be limited on some bodies, with firmware updates in development for others. Full details are on TTArtisan's product page.

Pricing and availability

The lens is available to preorder now at $489 in both mounts. One caption on the product page references an L-Mount version, but as yet there is no official word on its status.

entry.title: Insta360 Ace Pro 3 launch date: December 1 confirmed
entry.summary: 2 minute read Insta360 Ace Pro 3 launch date: December 1 confirmed 3:23 Insta360 will unveil the Ace Pro 3 in China on December 1. Its teaser points to interchangeable lenses, a variable aperture, and focus control. Well, this is a surprise. In the high-stakes game of next-genera
entry.content:
2 minute read
Insta360 Ace Pro 3 launch date: December 1 confirmed
3:23

Insta360 will unveil the Ace Pro 3 in China on December 1. Its teaser points to interchangeable lenses, a variable aperture, and focus control.

Well, this is a surprise. In the high-stakes game of next-generation action camera launches, which we confidently said earlier this month was on hold until next year, Insta360 has pulled the trigger on the Ace Pro 3.

Insta360's official Weibo account (weibo.com/insta360) posted a teaser video and key visual on the evening of November 24, tagged #影石acepro3# and promising an announcement on December 1 at 20:00 Beijing time (12:00 UTC). Nothing has appeared on Insta360's global channels or insta360.com yet, which might point to this being a China-only announcement with the global launch coming later, perhaps to coincide with CES 2027 (January 6 to 9).

Insta360 and DJI both used this tactic during the long, drawn-out launches of the Luna and Pocket 4 series gimbal cameras. Effectively, the Chinese release provides a soft launch to the rest of the world, which the companies then circle back to with the official global launch later.

So, while the announcement is now set for December, the global rollout and availability may well slip into next year. Which, we guess, means we might have been right about the 2027 thing after all…

What the Ace Pro 3 teaser reveals

The tagline "定局已破" loosely translates as "the mold is broken", or overturning something everyone took as settled. Getting a decent-quality upload of the Weibo video isn't easy from outside China, so here's leaker Igor Bogdanov's share of it, which provides the best quality we've got so far.

👉Well, hello, @insta360 Ace Pro 3. Long time no see 🫣 https://t.co/am7X3Q8Jrn

— Igor Bogdanov (@Quadro_News) November 24, 2026

Breaking the mold seems about right. The teaser gives four clues: bokeh, variable aperture, interchangeable lenses, and focusing. Some of these have appeared on action cameras before, with the DJI Osmo Action 6 bringing a variable aperture and the GoPro Mission 1 Pro ILS swappable lenses, but all four together really would be something else.

The key visual, meanwhile, shows three different lens heads: a domed element under a petal-style hood, an octagonal lens with Leica branding and a partial "ASPH." marking, and a third dome with a red accent ring.

Taken together, the clues point to a versatile all-rounder in a very compact body.

Ace Pro 3 rumored specs and price

Unsurprisingly, the rumor mill has kicked into top gear. 8K30 and 50 MP stills are being talked about fairly consistently, and the pricing mentioned is around the $549 to $599 region. This is significantly up from the $399 of the Ace Pro 2, but, given the new capabilities, is about what you'd expect.

Insta360 founder JK Liu has said on Chinese social media that the goal is that users don't need to carry a second camera with them for different tasks. If the company has nailed some of the technical challenges that come with cramming so much into a still-small form factor, they might not need to.

entry.title: Nikon ZR firmware 2.00 out now: full feature list and what is still to come
entry.summary: 3 minute read Nikon ZR firmware 2.00 out now: full feature list and what is still to come 5:53 Nikon's free ZR firmware 2.00 brings RED color science to H.265 through Log3G10. Open gate and anamorphic desqueeze are promised for 2027. After being heavily trailed and receiving as m
entry.content:
3 minute read
Nikon ZR firmware 2.00 out now: full feature list and what is still to come
5:53

Nikon's free ZR firmware 2.00 brings RED color science to H.265 through Log3G10. Open gate and anamorphic desqueeze are promised for 2027.

After being heavily trailed and receiving as many press releases as some entire cameras get, Nikon ZR firmware 2.00 is available to download from today, November 24. The headlines are that it brings RED color science to the camera's compact H.265 recordings, while also holding out the promise of more to come. Open gate recording and a desqueeze display for anamorphic lenses are not part of the update, but Nikon says both are in development for next year.

What arrives now

The main addition is Log3G10 gamma in the H.265 tone mode options, which enables recording in the REDWideGamutRGB gamut. Until now, ZR owners wanting RED's color pipeline had to shoot R3D NE, the RAW format Nikon developed to carry it. Nikon says H.265 gives smaller files while keeping substantial room for grading.

The rest of the update is workflow-focused, and none the worse for it:

  • A selectable High ISO NR level, in four settings, for Log3G10 and N-Log recording in H.265, and for N-Log in ProRes 422 HQ
  • Focus peaking while recording R3D NE with a 3D LUT applied
  • A 3D LUT can now be applied to HDMI output
  • ISO, exposure compensation, white balance, and color temperature can be assigned to the command dials in M mode, and 3D LUT/View Assist can be assigned to an Fn button
  • Updated processing that Nikon says suppresses frame-by-frame black level fluctuations, reducing flicker in dark areas

While all very welcome, it's hard not to be slightly more excited by what is promised for 2027.

Open gate and desqueeze: what Nikon has promised for 2027

Nikon said in September that it is developing firmware for open gate recording and a desqueeze display for anamorphic lenses, "with the goal of incorporating them in ZR firmware in 2027." Unfortunately, that is as specific as Nikon has been, with no indication of precisely when in 2027 or further detail about how it will all work, such as which open gate recording modes will be offered.

Nikon itself describes both as frequently requested features, and this is unsurprising. Open gate's ability to reframe post-shoot or deliver to multiple aspect ratios from one recording is almost tailor-made for modern briefs, while a desqueeze display makes working with anamorphic lenses much easier. In an ideal world, for a camera with the ambitions of the ZR, both should have been there from launch. There is speculation that the ZR's fanless body may be part of the reason open gate was missing, though Nikon has not confirmed this.

RED CONTROL apps and NIKKOR cinema lenses

Nikon also said in September that RED is updating its RED CONTROL and RED CONTROL PRO apps to add remote control of the ZR. At the time of writing, neither lists the ZR among supported cameras, though that may well change as the earth rotates and the US comes online today.

The wider RED and Nikon picture is also filling in. Nikon has nine NIKKOR Z CINEMA T1.9 VV lenses in development, starting with a 50mm. This has been a long time coming. The video below was released earlier this year and, as we noted in September, the 50mm may not arrive until around NAB 2027, never mind the following eight.

 

They will be worth waiting for, though. The lenses will have an image circle large enough to cover Nikon's full-frame sensors as well as the VistaVision (VV) format and the 40.96 mm × 21.60 mm (1.61 in × 0.85 in) image sensor of RED's V-RAPTOR [X], a first for NIKKOR lenses. They will also include an autofocus mechanism alongside manual focus control.

Firmware 2.00 is a free download from Nikon's ZR firmware page. The full changelog is below.

Full changelog from v1.11

Video Recording

  • Added [Log3G10] to the tone mode options available when video file type is set to [H.265 10-bit (MOV)].
  • 3D LUT can now be applied to video output via HDMI.
  • Focus peaking is now available when 3D LUT is set to ON.
  • Reduced noise in dark areas of videos.
  • [High ISO NR] is now available with [N-Log] tone mode when video file type is set to [H.265 10-bit (MOV)] or [ProRes 422 HQ 10-bit (MOV)].
  • Changed the following item names in Picture Controls:
    • [Cloud Picture Control] changed to [Imaging Recipe].
    • [Add Cloud Picture Control files] under [Set Picture Control] in the [VIDEO RECORDING MENU] changed to [Download Imaging Recipes].

Still Photography

  • Changed the following item names in Picture Controls:
    • [Cloud Picture Control] changed to [Imaging Recipe].
    • [Add Cloud Picture Control files] under [Set Picture Control] in the [PHOTO SHOOTING MENU] changed to [Download Imaging Recipes].

Controls

  • Made the following changes to the [CUSTOM SETTINGS MENU]:
    • Added b4 [Easy ISO].
    • Exposure compensation, ISO sensitivity, white balance, and color temperature can now be assigned to the command dials in mode M using [Command dials] > [Exposure setting] under f2 [Custom controls (shooting)] and g2 [Custom controls].
    • Added [3D LUT/View assist] as an assignable role to g2 [Custom controls].
    • Added g12 [Easy exposure compensation].

Other Changes

  • [Save] in [SETUP MENU] > [Manage user settings] is now [Edit].
  • Fixed an issue where scrolling with touch controls was not smooth when live view was zoomed in with the camera in tall orientation and [Auto-rotate pictures] set to OFF.

Changelog text: Nikon.

Understanding team communication needs in modern production

Wireless intercom systems have become essential for seamless collaboration across film production, live streaming, broadcasting, and on-site events. The market is increasingly favoring systems that are easy to deploy, cost-effective, and adaptable to varying crew sizes. When selecting a wireless intercom, key considerations include the number of team members, communication range, interference resistance, environmental noise cancellation, and overall budget.

A new, lower-priced version of the popular Fujifilm GFX Eterna 55 is being listed on both sides of the Atlantic.

As spotted by Fuji Rumors, B&H Photo is now listing a body-only version of the Fujifillm GFX Eterna 55 at $9999, against $16,499 for the original configuration, which is still on sale alongside it.

In the UK, CVP is taking pre-orders for the body at £9499 including VAT (£7915 ex VAT), with stock expected on November 27. CVP lists the contents as the camera body, battery, body cap, and PL mount adapter. The original package also included an LCD monitor and power adapter. The top handle is not listed in CVP's box contents either.

TheEterna 55 uses a 102 MP, 43.8 x 32.9 mm (1.72 x 1.30 in) sensor with dual base ISO of 800 and 3200, and an electronic variable ND filter covering ND0.6 to ND2.1 (roughly 2 to 7 stops). It weighs 2 kg (4.4 lb) and is IMAX-certified. It launched in September 2025 at $16,499 and £13,999.

Fujifilm has not yet commented on the new pricing, and we're not sure the missing components account for the whole $6500 difference. It's tempting to think that it's just a Black Friday deal, but the 'new item' and pre-order status suggest something a bit more permanent.

entry.summary: 1 minute read Kodak SlideTag: price, specs, and tracking 1:57 Reto's Kodak SlideTag is a work of slight genius and combines a $34.99 keychain with an E Ink photo screen and Apple and Google device tracking. Just in time for Christmas, Kodak licensee Reto, the company behind the z
entry.content:
1 minute read
Kodak SlideTag: price, specs, and tracking
1:57

Reto's Kodak SlideTag is a work of slight genius and combines a $34.99 keychain with an E Ink photo screen and Apple and Google device tracking.

Just in time for Christmas, Kodak licensee Reto, the company behind the zeitgeist-friendly hit Charmera camera, has launched the Kodak SlideTag, a clever little device that mashes together three things and thus becomes an impressive small object of desire.

It is a keychain with an AirTag-like Bluetooth tracker, it is a customizable E Ink display that will display your own photos, and it is a heady nostalgic trip for anyone who remembers the mingled joy and horror of family slide shows. It is a fourth thing as well, a blind box, but nothing's perfect.

Nine designs are available that all recreate the cardboard-and-plastic slide mounts that Kodachrome made familiar from 1935 onward and that were stored in shoeboxes under beds everywhere. They are built around a 1.54-inch, 6-color E Ink display at 240 x 240 pixels. Photos are loaded through the KODAK Memory Link app, which also handles slideshows, QR codes, and to-do lists.

The tracking works with Apple Find My and Google Find Hub with an approximate range of up to 30 m (98 ft) in open air, and the tag can sound off at 75 dB to help you find it and whatever essential equipment it's attached to.

It is small and light at 39.3 x 46 x 7.58 mm (1.55 x 1.81 x 0.30 in) and 16.6 g (0.6 oz), and has an IP54 rating so it will handle splashes and dust but is not waterproof. It runs on a replaceable CR2032 coin cell.

Pricing and availability

Like the Charmera, the SlideTag is sold as a blind box, at $34.99. There are eight standard designs plus one secret edition with a 1/64 chance, while a whole set of eight is currently $210. Reto says that one of the basic editions will be replaced if the secret edition appears in the set.

entry.title: OZ Racing’s Rally Legend campaign shot on Blackmagic 12K
entry.summary: 3 minute read OZ Racing’s Rally Legend campaign shot on Blackmagic 12K 5:49 Cinematographers Paolo Concari and Jacopo Cosmelli took two 12K Blackmagic cameras and a set of vintage Leica R lenses up the Apuan Alps for OZ Racing’s Rally Legend wheels. [ Blackmagic sent us this one
entry.content:
3 minute read
OZ Racing’s Rally Legend campaign shot on Blackmagic 12K
5:49

Cinematographers Paolo Concari and Jacopo Cosmelli took two 12K Blackmagic cameras and a set of vintage Leica R lenses up the Apuan Alps for OZ Racing’s Rally Legend wheels.

[Blackmagic sent us this one in and we liked it enough that we're publishing it pretty much as is. Ed]

OZ Racing’s Rally Legend “Keep Exploring” campaign took cinematographers Paolo Concari and Jacopo Cosmelli to Tuscany’s Apuan Alps, where they used Blackmagic URSA Cine 12K LF and PYXIS 12K digital film cameras to film a Jeep Wrangler JK fitted with the Italian manufacturer’s new off-road wheels.

The commercial follows the Jeep across paved roads, dirt tracks, and rugged terrain before shifting its attention to a nature filmmaker exploring the landscape on foot.

One look, different shoots

“From a cinematographic standpoint, the challenge was to maintain strong visual consistency while constantly shifting between very different shooting situations,” says Cosmelli. “From vast Alpine landscapes to high frame rates of the wheels, and onboard footage, we had to move quickly between different focal lengths, camera movements, and points of view.”

While the PYXIS 12K was used for much of the landscape photography, close-ups, and moving shots, the URSA Cine 12K LF came into its own for the slow-motion footage of the wheels. “Having the same RGBW sensor technology in both cameras gave us excellent color detail, along with 16 stops of dynamic range,” Concari says. “It also meant the footage matched naturally, giving Cosmelli a consistent starting point and plenty of flexibility in color grading.”

The PYXIS 12K was rigged with a Blackmagic PYXIS Monitor, a Blackmagic PYXIS Pro Handle, a SmallRig Mini Matte Box, a video transmitter, and a RØDE boom mic. “Despite the additional accessories, the setup remained easy to work with, particularly for handheld shots following the protagonist on foot and during the driving sequences,” he explains.

“The URSA Cine 12K LF was equipped with the 5-inch HDR touchscreen monitor, Blackmagic URSA Cine Handle, and Blackmagic URSA Cine EVF, along with a NiSi Cinema C5 Matte Box.

Vintage Leica glass and a third camera

“We also used the Micro Studio Camera 4K G2 for the shots mounted on the Jeep and the FPV drone, where we needed something much smaller,” Concari added. “Both the URSA Cine and PYXIS were paired with vintage Leica R lenses, ranging from 19mm to 60mm Macro.

“We chose them for their organic rendering. They’re sharp without feeling overly clinical, with lovely microcontrast and natural bokeh. For the scenes where the actor leaves the Jeep and continues on foot, we mostly used the 24mm and 35mm on the PYXIS, shooting in 8K 3:2 at 25 fps. Those wider lenses gave us room to show the scale of the mountains without losing the character in the frame.”

For a scene with the actor standing close to the Jeep during the blue hour, Cosmelli switched to the 60mm Macro lens.

“We wanted to get closer to his face and pick up the smaller expressions, but we also had to be careful with the exposure,” he says. “He was standing in shade with a bright sky and mountains behind him. We shot at ISO 800 and used false color and the histogram to judge how far we could go without losing detail in his face or the highlights.”

For the automotive sequences, the URSA Cine 12K LF captured the Rally Legend wheels as the Jeep crossed water and loose terrain.

“We shot mainly handheld, although we also relied on a Manfrotto tripod for more controlled shots,” says Cosmelli. “We used the 24mm Leica R quite a bit, shooting 8K 3:2 Open Gate and switching to 2.4:1 when we wanted to go up to 224 fps.

“The water crossings were probably the trickiest because you never quite knew how the water was going to behave. The same with the dry leaves. We’d have one chance to catch it as the Jeep came through, so getting the timing right was important. Those shots were difficult to control because everything happened so quickly. Being able to push the frame rate meant we could really see what was happening around the wheels.”

Small cameras for tight spots

For onboard footage, the production used the Blackmagic Micro Studio Camera 4K G2, mounting it to the side, hood, and rear of the Jeep with Tilta suction cup mounts and a Manfrotto Super Clamp 035C. A Cinekinetic Cinesaddle was used to get the camera really low, right down beside the wheels. The team also flew the camera on a custom-built 178 mm (7 in) X4 FPV cinelifter drone, using either a Leica R 19mm lens with a Metabones adapter or a Laowa 7.5mm lens.

“The size of the Micro Studio Camera meant we could put it in places where the larger cameras wouldn’t fit,” Cosmelli concludes. “We could get right up close to the action with the camera mounted on the Jeep, then use it on the FPV drone for much wider shots, still recording Blackmagic RAW directly to a SanDisk SSD connected via USB-C in both setups.”

The team edited, graded, and delivered the campaign in DaVinci Resolve Studio.

Production credits

  • Directors and Directors of Photography: Paolo Concari and Jacopo Cosmelli
  • Producers: Paolo Concari and Jacopo Cosmelli
  • Editor and Colorist: Jacopo Cosmelli
  • Still Photographer: Filippo Maffei
  • FPV Pilot: Gabriele Montagni
  • Drone Pilot: Leonardo Cantarelli
  • VO Author: Jacopo Pozzi
  • VO Actor: Beau Davidson
  • Precision Driver: Matteo Delbono
  • Original Music: Alessandro Franceschini
  • Camera Equipment Supplied By: Adcom Srl

entry.summary: 2 minute read DJI Osmo Pocket 4 price rise in China: up to 13% 3:36 Rises of up to 13% have hit DJI's best-selling pocket gimbal cameras in China, blamed on memory costs. While global buyers currently see Black Friday discounts, the increases are likely to spread. RAMageddon cont
entry.content:
2 minute read
DJI Osmo Pocket 4 price rise in China: up to 13%
3:36

Rises of up to 13% have hit DJI's best-selling pocket gimbal cameras in China, blamed on memory costs. While global buyers currently see Black Friday discounts, the increases are likely to spread.

RAMageddon continues. At the same time that DJI is highlighting the savings across its range in the annual Black Friday sales, especially on previous-generation kit, the company has raised the prices of its Osmo Pocket 4, Osmo Pocket 4P, and Osmo Nano in China, by as much as 13% on some bundles. It's the latest in a string of memory-driven price rises across the camera industry this year.

DJI announced the move on November 13 in a short notice on its China website, titled "Explanation Regarding Adjustments to Suggested Retail Prices for Certain DJI Products." It blamed sustained, sharp increases in the cost of key components, including semiconductors and memory, and said new suggested retail prices would apply from midnight Beijing time on November 18.

The notice didn't say which products, or by how much. That information came from a piece in Beijing Daily, the company telling the paper that the changes covered some of its handheld gimbal cameras and thumb cameras currently on sale, and that the aim was to ensure normal supply and stable product quality.

This all makes sense. The Pocket 4, for example, has 107 GB of storage built in, and the Nano also relies on onboard memory. That makes them far more exposed to NAND pricing variations than a typical camera that offloads storage to a card.

What's gone up and by how much

Chinese pricing does not always map onto that seen in other countries, so the percentages are the better guide here. The Osmo Pocket 4P Standard Combo went from RMB 3799 to RMB 4099 (about 8%), while the Pocket 4P Vlog Combo took the biggest hit, rising RMB 560 to RMB 4859 (13%, or roughly $83 more).

The standard Osmo Pocket 4 rose from RMB 2999 to RMB 3199 (about 7%). Several of its bundles climbed further, with the All-in-One and Meipai kits each up RMB 500, to RMB 4299 (about 13%) and RMB 4598 (about 12%) respectively. The Enjoy Shooting kit escaped with a smaller RMB 140 rise to RMB 3638 (about 4%).

The Osmo Nano split down the middle: the 128 GB version rose RMB 200 to RMB 2498 (about 9%), while the 64 GB version stays at RMB 1998. That detail rather neatly tells you where the cost pressure is coming from.

Not everything is moving. DJI launched the Osmo 360 II in China at the same price as its predecessor.

Will prices elsewhere follow?

DJI’s Black Friday sale is a dynamic one with plenty of moving parts. In terms of the products that we know are affected in China, in the UK, for example, currently we’re seeing 8% off the Osmo Pocket 4P Standard Combo in the UK and 5% off the Pocket 4. After Black Friday is over, we’ll just have to see if those prices head back to where they were or overshoot to the new Chinese level.

As yet, arch-rival Insta360 had not responded, though the company's third-quarter results showed profits falling, with rising memory component costs cited as a significant factor. If memory prices behave as the industry expects next year, stabilizing at best, DJI is unlikely to be the last company to raise prices.

entry.summary: 4 minute read Best 360 Cameras 2026: X6 vs Osmo 360 II vs Max 2 7:11 The best 360 cameras of 2026 are the Insta360 X6, DJI Osmo 360 II, and GoPro Max 2. Here is how they compare. Last year's guide pitted the Insta360 X5, GoPro Max 2, and DJI Osmo 360 against each other. A year on
entry.content:
4 minute read
Best 360 Cameras 2026: X6 vs Osmo 360 II vs Max 2
7:11

The best 360 cameras of 2026 are the Insta360 X6, DJI Osmo 360 II, and GoPro Max 2. Here is how they compare.

Last year's guide pitted the Insta360 X5, GoPro Max 2, and DJI Osmo 360 against each other. A year on, Insta360 has launched the X6 and DJI has launched the Osmo 360 II, which leaves the Max 2 as the only one of the three 360 cameras that has not been updated. Despite the well-reviewed Mission 1 series, GoPro itself is in flux: it has agreed a $285 million merger with Starman Optical that looks more like a takeover, which makes a successor to the Max 2 hard to predict.

The X6 went on sale worldwide on 12 August at $699, which is $150 more than the X5 cost at launch. The Osmo 360 II launched in China on 13 August and globally on 3 September, with sales starting on 15 September. It costs £509 ($571) in the UK against £619 for the X6, but, as we are all too well aware, DJI has no official US availability.

Simon Wyndham has reviewed all three, so here is a snapshot of which one best suits your needs with the holiday shopping season fast approaching.

360-camera cheat sheet

The X6 leads on battery life, the Osmo 360 II on price and storage, and the Max 2 on toughness and helmet-friendly size, despite now being over a year old.

Spec Insta360 X6 DJI Osmo 360 II GoPro Max 2
Release date 12 August 2026 13 August 2026 (China); on sale globally 15 September 2026 23 September 2025 (announced)
Price $699 / £619 / €699 £509 / from €589 (about $571); no official US sale $499 at launch; about $299 in Black Friday sales
Sensors Dual 1/1.1-inch square Dual 1/1.1-inch square Dual 1/2.3-inch
Top frame rates 8K50 (360); 5K60 and 4K120 (single lens) 8K60 and 4K240 (360) 8K30, 5.6K60, and 4K100 (360); 4K60 (single lens)
Stills 120 MP (360); 42 MP (flat) 120 MP (360); 30.72 MP (flat) 29 MP (360); 12 MP (flat)
Log and color I-Log (360 modes and InstaFrame 2.0 only) and Dolby Vision; 10-bit D-Log M (not full D-Log); 10-bit GP-Log; 10-bit
Weight 196 g (6.9 oz) 183 g (6.5 oz) 195 g (6.9 oz)
Dimensions 50 × 100 × 40 mm (2.0 × 3.9 × 1.6 in) 61 × 36.3 × 81 mm (2.4 × 1.4 × 3.2 in) 69.7 × 64 × 48.7 mm (2.7 × 2.5 × 1.9 in)
Waterproof to 20 m (66 ft); 60 m (197 ft) with dive case 10 m (33 ft); 50 m (164 ft) with dive case 5 m (16 ft)
Battery 2600 mAh; 140 min at 8K30 2150 mAh; 100 min at 8K30 1960 mAh; just over 60 min at 8K
Fast charging 80% in 24 min 80% in 22 min None
Built-in storage 47 GB usable 105 GB usable None (microSD only)
Display 2.32-inch OLED 2.0-inch, 800 nits 1.82-inch touchscreen
Strengths Large 1/1.1-inch sensors; 8K50 360 video; longest battery life with fast charging; in-camera Dolby Vision; 10-bit I-Log, including in low light; 360, tracking gimbal, and single-lens modes in one body £110 cheaper than the X6; 105 GB onboard storage; 8K60; replaceable lenses; D-Log M in single-lens modes; strong low light; Spotlight Follow tracking Tough lenses that swap in seconds; true 8K with a gradable 10-bit image; compact, low-profile body; lowest price; built-in GPS
Weaknesses Highest price, $150 above the X5; still tall for helmets, and X5 brackets do not fit; I-Log limited to 360 modes and InstaFrame 2.0, and 24p limited to 360 modes; Adaptive Tone 2 HDR processing cannot be turned off, causing halos in the standard profile Haloing in bright light (shoot at -1 EV); warping behind foreground objects; 4K240 too noisy to use; no official US sale Just over an hour of 8K recording; no fast charging; weaker low light; Bluetooth wireless audio limited to 16 kHz; GoPro's future unclear while its Starman Optical merger is pending
Best for Creators who want strong low light, long battery life, and on-camera AI editing in one body DJI users, and anyone who wants log recording and big storage for less than the X6 Helmet POV and adventure shooters who risk their gear and want top image quality
More detail Insta360 X6 review (YouTube) Osmo 360 II review Max 2 review

In summary: it all depends on your priorities

None of the three is perfect, but each lines up well with a different set of priorities.

  • Low light and battery life: The choice comes down to the X6 and the Osmo 360 II. The X6 runs longer on a charge (140 minutes of 8K30 against 100) and offers in-camera Dolby Vision and 10-bit I-Log, including in its low-light mode. The Osmo 360 II costs £110 less, has more than double the onboard storage, charges slightly faster, and records log in single-lens modes too. Both apply HDR-style processing that can cause haloing: Adaptive Tone 2 cannot be switched off on the X6, and the Osmo 360 II needs -1 EV in bright light to tame it.
  • Helmet POV and rough use: The Max 2 is the one to beat. Our reviewer rates it the best 360 camera for POV because of its low profile, and its lenses can be replaced in seconds in the field, though it manages just over an hour of 8K and falls behind in low light. The X6 is shorter than the X5 but still tall for a helmet. The X5's horizontal bracket does not fit it, and the horizontal bracket Insta360 has since released comes with some restrictions.
  • Lifestyle, vlogging, and adventure: The X6 can cover all three, provided you can live with I-Log being limited to 360 modes and InstaFrame 2.0, and 24p to 360 modes. Our reviewer hopes a firmware update will open both up to the other single-lens modes.
  • Price and availability: The Max 2 is the cheapest at about $299 in Black Friday sales (it launched at $499), but GoPro's own future is uncertain while its merger with Starman Optical is pending. The Osmo 360 II has no official US sale, which leaves the X6 and the Max 2 as the practical options for US buyers.

A caution from our review worth repeating: 360 footage needs extra processing and editing steps, so for most people these remain specialist cameras to add alongside a traditional action camera, although new Insta360 and DJI models may not arrive until spring 2027.

entry.title: Black Friday 2026 deals: part one
entry.summary: 7 minute read Black Friday 2026 deals: part one 13:28 Part one of our Black Friday 2026 deals coverage: the early offers on cameras, drones, lenses, editing software, and streaming kit for filmmakers. Black Friday falls on November 27 this year, with Cyber Monday on November 30.
entry.content:
7 minute read
Black Friday 2026 deals: part one
13:28

Part one of our Black Friday 2026 deals coverage: the early offers on cameras, drones, lenses, editing software, and streaming kit for filmmakers.

Black Friday falls on November 27 this year, with Cyber Monday on November 30. Many manufacturers and resellers have started early, some as far back as October, so this first round-up covers the offers live now and those starting soon. More deals will follow as the main event approaches.

The big resellers

Always worth checking out the big guys as they have massive product lines and an at times bewildering number of offers. Many of you will probably take a look at Amazon as well. It carries a load of offers but can often play rather fast and loose with what it considers to be a sale price. We found a Sony a7C II 'deal' that had been the same price a further four times this year. The price history button here is your friend.

Adorama deals | B&H deals | CVP deals | Wex Photo Video deals

Best Black Friday 2026 camera deals: RED, Nikon, Panasonic, Sony

RED has cut the KOMODO-X 6K cinema camera body (Canon RF) to $4995, down from $6995, a $2000 saving at B&H. B&H also lists a KOMODO-X Starter Pack (V-Mount) at $8995, and CVP has the body at €4540 excluding VAT.

Another B&H listing has the Nikon Z8 body only at $3196, down from $4296, a $1100 saving listed as Holiday Savings at B&H. The listing includes extended returns through February 1, 2027.

Panasonic Lumix GH5 II body only is $997, down from $1497, saving $500 (33%) at Adorama.

CVP has the Sony FX3 Full-Frame Cinema Camera listed at £2499, down from £2999, including VAT. The camera got a big boost in the market while the FX5 was delayed, and is a capable unit, especially at that price.

Sony also holds the prize for the biggest discount we've seen this round, with B&H listing the Sony PMW-F5 CineAlta Digital Cinema Camera for $4390, a massive $12,100 off the list price.

Best Black Friday 2026 lenses and optics deals: DZOFILM, SIRUI, Viltrox

DZOFILM has a Black Friday sale running October 20 to December 3, with up to $2989 off the Arles Prime 10-lens kit. The Arcana Anamorphic 3-lens kit is $2699, down from $2899 (November 5 to December 1). Vespid Prime 2 starts at $999, down from $1199, and Pavo 2X Anamorphic starts at $2299, down from $3399, up to 38% off.

SIRUI has a Black Friday sale at its official store from November 16 to November 30, with up to 80% off lenses, tripods, and lighting. SIRUI says each offer runs to its own schedule, so check the end date on individual products. Some of the offers are genuinely impressive. For example, you can get the Saturn 35/50/75mm T2.9 1.6x Full-Frame Carbon Fiber Anamorphic Lenses for $399 each, a 69% saving on their usual $1299.

Viltrox has up to 20% off from November 19 to November 30, with discounts varying by product. Gift tiers apply after discounts, and an 8K HDMI cable is $5 during the sale. The recently launched AF 35mm F1.4 Pro is available at its launch-day promotional price. The final checkout cutoff is December 1 at 15:00 Beijing time. Details on the Viltrox Black Friday lens guide.

Best Black Friday 2026 drones and gimbals deals: Antigravity, DJI

Antigravity says its Black Friday discounts on the A1 drone are its biggest to date, running November 19 to December 7. The Standard Bundle (regular $1599) is 31% off, about $1103, while the Explorer Bundle (regular $1899) and Infinity Bundle (regular $1999) are 35% off, about $1234 and $1299. The Follow Me Bundle is 25% off and the Follow Me Accessory Kit 20% off. Eligible purchases also qualify for a gift pack worth up to $174 on registration. Details on the Antigravity Black Friday page.

DJI has up to 28% off its products, which brings the likes of the entry-level DJI Neo down 18% to £119 in the UK and the still extremely capable Osmo Pocket 3 down 15% to £262. The sale currently seems to cover older product lines, but looks set to introduce new offers as we move towards Cyber Monday. Deals also seem to be per territory, so are worth checking out individually.

Best Black Friday 2026 action camera deals: DJI, GoPro, Insta360

Insta360 has its official Black Friday sale from November 19 to December 1, with up to £164 off selected bundles on the UK store and free accessories worth up to £24.99. Examples: X6 Essentials Bundle £635, down from £709, Ace Pro 2 Standard Bundle £279, down from £409, and GO 3S Standard Bundle £239, down from £369. Price protection covers purchases from November 6 to December 27.

DJI Osmo Action 4 Essential Combo is £159 at Amazon UK, down from £199 (20% off), tagged as a Black Friday deal. As indicated above, this is unlikely to be the only DJI deal you'll see this holiday season.

GoPro's sale leads with $200 off the MAX2, but there's also money off its newer cameras too with $100 off the Mission 1 Pro series and associated bundles, though as yet the Mission 1 Pro ILS does not seem to be included, which is a shame. Still, the Mission 1 Pro Grip Edition for $679 is a bit of a steal.

Best Black Friday 2026 post and VFX deals: Adobe, Avid, Beeble, DxO, Time in Pixels

Post seems to be particularly active this year, and we start with Adobe, which has 57% off Creative Cloud Pro for first-time individual subscribers, from November 13 to November 27. In the US, the annual plan billed monthly is $29.99 a month (regular $69.99), and the annual prepaid plan is $334 for the first year (regular $779). Both need a 12-month commitment and renew at the then-current price. Creative Cloud Pro includes Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Acrobat Pro, InDesign, and 4000 monthly generative credits. UK customers pay £28.49 a month or £331 prepaid, including VAT. Details on Adobe's offer terms.

Avid has Media Composer annual subscriptions on sale through November 29. Media Composer Standard is $208 a year (regular $259, 20% off) and Media Composer Ultimate is $362 a year (regular $539, 33% off). The offer applies to new purchases of the one-year, paid-upfront subscription only, and renews at standard pricing. The sale also covers Pro Tools Artist, Pro Tools Studio, Pro Tools Ultimate, Sibelius Artist, and Sibelius Ultimate. More at Avid.

Beeble has 30% off annual plans and 20% off monthly plans for new customers from November 16 to November 30, excluding additional credits and Enterprise plans. The offer arrives alongside the launch of SwitchX 3.0, its AI video-to-video model, which is included in all paid plans with no change to credit pricing. Details at Beeble.

DxO has Black Friday prices across its whole range from November 17 to November 29, with up to 50% off. FilmPack 8 is half price. Nik Collection 9 is $149 (was $179), and PureRAW 6 is $99.99 (was $139). No codes are needed, and offers cover new licenses and eligible upgrades. Buy via DxO.

Time in Pixels, maker of the Nobe OmniScope video scopes software, is offering 30% off everything on its site with code SCOPESBF2026, from November 25 to December 2. OmniScope Pro lists at €325 and the Live Pack add-on at €128.

Best Black Friday 2026 lighting deals: Nanlite

Some impressive savings from Nanlite, headed by steep pricing cuts in its PavoTube II 30C 4-Foot Full-Color LED Tube Light, which falls from $319 to $199. There's plenty more elsewhere too, with $70 off the FC-120C LED Full-Color Spotlight, which comes down to $269, and $150 off the FC-720B LED Bi-Color Spotlight, which drops to $499.

Best Black Friday 2026 storage and battery deals: Anton/Bauer, Core SWX, Sonnet

Anton/Bauer has up to 33% off Titon and Titon Micro battery kits in V-Mount and Gold Mount, and over 80% off EDEN, in its Black Friday sale. Offers are available through authorized dealers while supplies last. Details on the Anton/Bauer site.

Decent savings to be had at Core SWX, with the NANO X Micro 98Wh Series dropping 37% to $179 and the 150Wh version falling 33% to $265. The XCell V-Mount series is down too, with the 99Wh falling 19% to $145 and the 150Wh one 20% to $205. The HyperCore G3 99 Series falls $100 to $299. Bundle three products together and save a further 5%.

Sonnet has up to 20% off a selection of Thunderbolt docks, display adapters, and storage accessories from November 16 to November 30 (PT). The Echo 21 Thunderbolt 5 SuperDock is $399 (was $499), the Echo 13 Thunderbolt 5 Dock is $239 (was $299), and the Tempo SSD PCIe Card is $39.99 (was $49.99). A certified refurbished Echo 20 Thunderbolt 4 SuperDock is $159 (was $199). Available from the Sonnet Store, Amazon, B&H, and other resellers.

Best Black Friday 2026 streaming deals: YoloLiv

YoloLiv has up to $200 off its streaming range, with the sale ending November 30. The YoloBox Extreme is $2099 (was $2299), the YoloBox Ultra is $1399 (was $1599), and the YoloCam S3 webcam is $199 (was $219). The sale also covers the YoloCam S7, YoloCast, and Network Bonding plans. Available from the YoloLiv official store and local resellers.

Best Black Friday 2026 monitors, recorders, and wireless deals: ASUS, EZCast

ASUS has taken 10% off the price of its popular ProArt Display PA329CRV, which brings it down to £629 in the UK at least. The ProArt Display PA328QV also gets a cut, down 12% to £439.

EZCast has its CamCast wireless HDMI transmitter at $136 (was $170) on Amazon US with code CAMCAST20, a 20% saving. The offer runs through November 30 (PT), is limited to one per customer, and lasts while the promotion budget does. EZCast says CamCast sends one HDMI feed to up to four phones or tablets over 5 GHz WiFi and also works as a USB-C webcam. An NP-F battery and HDMI cable are not included.

Best Black Friday 2026 camera accessories deals: SANDMARC, SmallRig

SANDMARC has 20% off sitewide, with code BF2026 from November 20 to November 28 and code CM2026 from November 29 to December 1. The company says it keeps fixed pricing the rest of the year, making this its only sitewide sale of the season. The range includes iPhone filmmaking lenses and filters, creator bags, Apple Watch bands, and leather cases. Find it on the SANDMARC Black Friday page.

SmallRig has a Black Friday Mega Sale from November 19 to November 30 with up to 40% off across more than 300 products, backed by a 30-day price guarantee. Free gifts are unlocked when you spend a certain amount ($109 gets you a free USB-C Magnetic Self-Coiling Charging Cable in the US, for instance). It's hitting some of its mainstream products with offers too, the SmallRig x Potato Jet TRIBEX CARBON II Carbon Fiber Tripod falling 32% to $541.

Best Black Friday 2026 audio deals: Native Instruments

Native Instruments has 50% off its software at the NI Online Shop from November 19 to December 31, calculated on the suggested retail price. Komplete 26, Absynth 6, and SuperStarSaw are discounted for the first time, and Kontakt 8, Maschine, Traktor Pro 4, and Guitar Rig are also half price. Products released after September 1, 2026 are excluded, except Massive XL at its introductory 50% pricing. Details on the NI deals page.

But wait, there's more...

More deals will follow in our next round-up. Got a tip on a standout discount? Email editor@redsharknews.com and we'll feature notable finds in our regular updates.
